BACONC PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. €s S. JUL 03 2024 MR. ANTONIO C. NAPALAN, JR. Executive Assistant IV Office of the Mayor Kawit, Cavite Dear Mr. Napalan: This has reference to the letter dated 24 April 2024 requesting for a legal opinion on the Revised Revenue Code of the Municipality of Kawit 2023. The following points of clarification were raised, to wit: (1) Is the Sangguniang Panlalawigan correct that Ordinance No. 26-S. 2023 or "The Revised Revenue Code of the Municipality of Kawit, Cavite 2023" is inconsistent and violative of the provisions of Sec. 191 of the LGC which prescribes that LGUs shall have the authority to adjust tax rates but not oftener than once every five years, considering that the amendments in Kawit Municipal Ordinance No. Ol- 2022 are for fees and charges and not taxes? (2) Can local fees and charges be adjusted more often than once every five years, considering the nature of their imposition which is regulatory and aimed to recover the cost of services rendered, as opposed to taxes which are income generating? (3) Can the Municipality of Kawit still implement Ordinance No. 26-S. 2023 even when it was not approved nor disapproved by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within the mandatory thirty (30) day review period and can now be deemed approved? Please be informed at the outset that this Department's duty is to implement the Local Govemment Code via, inter alia, the rendition of legal opinions. Legal opinions for that matter are executive constructions given by the government agency concerned on a particular view it is tasked to implement. However, legal opinions have limitations, such that they cannot be rendered on issues that require factual adjudication in view of some conflicting claimsl. Moreover, we are bound by this Department's Memorandum Order No. 2010-022 which provides that the Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: (I) Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concemed, and similar instances; DILG LO No. 24 s. 2005 2 Supplement to Memorandum Order No. 2010-01 dated 4 March 2010; 17 September 2010. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion, we elucidate. Anent the first and second issue, we respectfully submit that legislative acts enjoy the presumption of validity, and legislative bodies are presumed to have carried out their function regularly in enacting the said measures, pursuant to Rule 131 , Sec. 3(m) of the Rules of Court. The matter of validity of legislative enactments may be threshed out in the proper judicial proceeding, as only courts are empowered by law to finally determine the validity of the herein questioned measure3. Indeed, the only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance, or order is "beyond the powers conferred upon the council or president making the same." Absolutely no other ground is recognized by the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance, or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval of any resolution, ordinance, or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the scope of the legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative function of the municipal council or president. Such has been the consistent course of executive authority4. Anent the third point, the provisions of the LGC provide the following: SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. - (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the Sanggunian Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan shall forward to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in making its decision. (c) If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sangguniang Panialawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) If no action has been taken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. 3 Department in DILG Opinion No, 73-A s. 2019. Moday vs. CA, G.R. No. 107916 February 20, 1997. Page 2 Of 3

SECTION 58. Enforcement of Disapproved ordinances or Resolutions. - Any attempt to enforce any ordinance or any resolution approving the local development plan and public investment program, after the disapproval thereof, shall be sufficient ground for the suspension or dismissal of the official or employee concerned. The Department had on several occasions the opportunity to discuss the p[ower of the review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. We cite the salient portions of DILG No. Opinion No. 20 s. 2019 which dealt with the same subject matter. The Department had consistently opined that the phrase "take action" in Sec. 56 (d) should mean that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, within 30 days upon receipt Of the copy Of the ordinance, should have issued its legislative action in the form of a Resolution containing their disapproval in whole or in part any ordinance or resolution submitted to them for review. It is not enough that they be deliberated, debated and voted on the measure out to be reviewed because what is required of them is the enactment of a legislative document to formally and finally put to rest a given measure or issue. This document enacted is imbued with public interest, so much that it shall be the basis of the general public to rely upon in performing their respective obligations or asserting their rights in a given territory. Absent this document, all local legislative debates are left as silent records, thus unenforceable as against third persons. Thus, after the lapse of such 30-day period, and no Resolutions which shall contain the findings of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on review of the municipal ordinance was issued by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, it can be validly stated that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan failed to act within 30 days and the ordinance under review can be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. Thus, the failure of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to validly act on Ordinance No. 26- S. 2023 within the mandatory thirty (30) day review period presupposes that the ordinance is deemed approved and valid pursuant to Sec. 56 (d) of the LGC. Moreover, the enforcement of a disapproved ordinance shall be sufficient ground for the suspension and dismissal of the official or employee concemed as provided under the aforementioned law. Finally, this Department's opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter.
